subject: Throughput & 5xx surge after model v4.1-int8 rollout — urgent
messages:
From: Claire Yang <claire.yang@holocenefin.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <e.park@holocenefin.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Latency/5xx spike after model v4.1-int8 rollout (Holocene Prod)

Hi Mina —

We pushed the Redwood model upgrade (v4.1 + quant profile 'int8-fast') to our production dedicated pool at ~02:00 UTC this morning and immediately saw a regression:
- p95 latency jumped from ~180ms -> ~760ms (for our typical 512 token flows)
- sustained throughput drop ~35% vs baseline
- 5xx rate ~1.8% (was ~0.03% before rollout)

Attached are a small sample of request ids and a short trace from our monitoring (holocene_trace_0629.csv). Logs show many requests timing out on the inference stage; errors are 502/504 coming from the model worker layer.

This is a production-impacting outage for our conversational flow. We need immediate assistance: rollback or emergency mitigation, and an explanation of root cause. Our SRE (Ethan) is CC'd — we can give API keys or traces as needed.

Please escalate to your engineering team — we're expecting this to be a high priority on both sides.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Yang
Head of Platform Reliability
Holocene Financial

Hi Claire — thanks for the quick flag and the trace. We're treating this as an urgent escalation.

Immediate asks to help us triage faster:
- Can you share 3 example request IDs (the ones in the attached trace are great) and one full request payload (you can redact PII) — sample_request_48932.json from your trace would be ideal.
- Confirm whether the affected hosts are your Dedicated pool (yes?) and if you rotated any custom routing/edge config at the same time.
- Do you have a short window where we can run a canary rollback or route a small percentage of traffic to the prior model (v4.0) without impacting customers?

I've looped in Ben (runtime lead) and Marissa (CS) to coordinate. We'll spin up a runbook now:
- Hot mitigation: route traffic to v4.0 or set quant profile to a safe fallback (hold until we validate).
- Post-mortem: collect traces, kernel logs, and run microbenchmarks on your Dedicated hosts.

We're available for a quick sync at your convenience; Marissa will propose times.

—Mina
Senior Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: [Internal] Initial analysis — Holocene throughput/5xx spike

Quick summary of what I'm seeing from the initial traces (correlating with Holocene's CSV + our telemetry):
- After switching to v4.1 with 'int8-fast' quant profile, CPU on the host (controller) increased due to additional memcpy/transpose ops; GPU kernels also shifted to a fallback slow-path for certain sequence lengths.
- There is a repeated KV cache miss pattern for sequences > 384 tokens in the sample requests; that forces partial recompute each step and dramatically increases per-token work for those sessions.
- Error signatures match a saturation + request timeout pattern on the worker; timeouts convert to 502s/504s at the edge.

Hypothesis: the 'int8-fast' profile enables a set of fused kernels that we prefer for throughput, but on Holocene's Dedicated hardware (custom A100 config + slightly older driver) those fused kernels fall back to slower reference kernels, and combined with the KV cache alignment issue we see throughput collapse and latency blowup. In short: quant+kernel mismatch + cache alignment is the likely culprit.

Proposed immediate actions (hot path):
1) Route traffic for Holocene to the previous model variant (v4.0-fp16) OR to v4.1 with 'int8-safe' profile (no fused kernels) — this should restore latency/throughput within minutes.
2) If above isn't viable, perform a rollback of the v4.1 rollout for Holocene's Dedicated pool (we can do a per-host rollback).
3) Collect a deterministic microbenchmark (we'll run on a spare host) and reproduce: compare v4.0-fp16 vs v4.1-int8-fast vs v4.1-int8-safe.

I've attached a short perf trace and an example request payload from Claire's CSV for repro (holocene_trace_0629.csv, sample_request_48932.json).

I'll prepare a patch that disables the fused-kernel selection for this customer's pool as a hotfix if we can't safely route them. ETA for hotfix validation: 4-6 hours depending on repro.

Attachments: holocene_trace_0629.csv (text/csv), sample_request_48932.json (application/json), perf_heap_profile.pb (application/octet-stream)

Subject: Executive summary & proposed remediation plan — Holocene outage (v4.1 rollout)

Claire / Holocene Execs —

Executive summary: after the v4.1 + 'int8-fast' rollout to your Dedicated pool on 2026-06-29 02:00 UTC, Holocene observed sustained latency increases, throughput loss (~35%), and elevated 5xx rates. Our initial engineering analysis points to a combined issue of quant-profile kernel selection and KV cache alignment for longer sequences on your Dedicated host configuration.

Immediate remediation that we are executing now:
- Route 100% of production traffic for Holocene to v4.0-fp16 (completed at 08:05 UTC) — preliminary metrics show p95 returning toward baseline; monitoring continues.
- We have disabled fused-kernel selection for Holocene's pool as a precaution.
- Engineering (Ben) is running microbenchmarks and will deliver a validated safe int8 profile ('int8-safe') within 24 hours if possible.

Customer-facing commitments being offered:
- Expedited hotfix timeline: validation + staged re-rollout of int8-safe within 24 hours; full rollback will remain available if any signal reappears.
- Service credit proposal: 25% credit for the impacted hours (subject to contract scope) — draft credit will be provided in the follow-up.
- Post-mortem with root cause analysis and mitigations within 3 business days.

Attachments: redwood_action_log_0629.txt (action log), mutual_action_plan_HF.docx

We're available for a call now or at the scheduled 16:00 ET slot to walk through the plan and next steps. Apologies for the disruption — we know the impact to your customers is unacceptable and we're treating this as top priority.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Success, Redwood Inference
